Visions and Values
Empowering our children to achieve their ambitions
By working together in an exciting, creative and supportive Christian environment we will challenge and inspire every child to become highly literate, numerate, sociable and healthy, with a thirst for continued learning and a belief in their ability to become significant citizens.
Values:
The school aims to serve its community by providing an education of the highest quality within the context of Christian belief and practice.
The school actively promotes a set of shared values in which every pupil, teacher, parent and governor has an important part to play. Our core values are:
friendship service endurance thankfulness
hope forgiveness
We are also committed to the teaching of British Values. These can be found as part of our long- term planning in the curriculum section of this website.
Enmore Church of England Primary School is a Limited Company by Guarantee. All Governors are directors of the company and as such have all agreed and signed the following statement to uphold the object of the Company in acting in their roles as governors.
"We recognise that the object of the Company is to establish, maintain, carry on, manage and develop the school with a designated Church of England religious character offering a broad and balanced curriculum to be conducted in accordance with the principles, practices and tenets of the Church of England both generally and in particular in relation to arranging for religious education and daily acts of worship (as required by the funding agreement) and in having regard to the advice of the Diocesan Board of Education."
We encourage members of our school community to advocate for others, show compassion and make a positive difference in our world.
We have achieved our FairAware School award.
Access- opportunities offered to all.

pageCache.text:
Breakfast and Afterschool Club.
Breakfast Club is available daily from 8am until the start of school at 8:45am.
After school club is available from 3:30pm until 5pm daily.
Children booked in beyond 4:30pm will be offered a tea selection of healthy items.
Booking children into sessions is completed online.
We are registered and set up to accept ChildCare vouchers from the following sources:
If your Childcare Voucher scheme provider is not listed, please let us know.
HM Government Tax Free Childcare scheme
Sodexo ChildCare Voucher Scheme
Edenred ChildCare Voucher Scheme
FairCare Childcare Voucher Scheme
Care4 Childcare Voucher Scheme
RG Childcare Voucher Scheme
Childcare Vouchers Scheme is particularly popular tax-free benefit, offering a great way to support working parents. When the Government Tax Free Childcare scheme was introduced, many of the other voucher schemes were closed to new entrants in September 2018, but do remain in place for users registered before then.
Below is a link to the Government Tax-Free Childcare scheme, where you can check your eligibility and apply for tax free childcare.
For every £8 you pay into your Tax Free ChildCare account Government will top this up with £2, up to the value of £2,000 per year per child. (or £4,000 for disabled children).

Board of Governors
The Academy Trust is a company limited by guarantee and an exempt charity. The Charitable Company's memorandum and articles of association are the primary governing documents of the academy trust. The Governors act as the trustees for the charitable activities of Enmore Church of England Primary School and are also the Directors of the Charitable company for the purposes of Company law.
It is a requirement of our Funding Agreement with the Education Skills & Funding Agency (ESFA) that in the interests of transparency we must publish up to date details of our governance arrangements.
The Governing Body is supported by its six committees, membership of which is derived from within its own Body. The constitution, membership, terms of reference and delegated powers of the committees are reviewed and approved annually and recorded in the school's "Standing Orders".
Governing Body and Annual General meeting minutes are available on request, please contact peaglestone-gunter@enmoreprimaryschool.org
For each member and trustee who has served at any point over the past 12 months, their full names, date of appointment, date they stepped down (where applicable), and relevant business and pecuniary interests including governance roles in other educational institutions are listed below.
Membership of both the Pupil Discipline and Staff Dismissal Appeal Sub-Committees will consist of three governors taken from the pool of governors who are eligible to stand on that particular committee.
The Governors at Enmore Primary School believe it is important that the board reflects the diversity of the school communities they serve. Diverse boards promote inclusive school environments and provide diverse role models for staff and young people.
The Governors are currently collecting data on the diversity of the board, including data on age, gender and ethnicity. They will use that data to inform their recruitment and training needs and ensure a diverse range of perspectives around the table to support robust decision-making.
Due to our relatively small governing body, we do not publish this diversity data online as individual governors could be identified and we have a legal obligation to protect their personal data.
Chair of Governing Body: Mrs. L. Smith
Safeguarding Governor: Mrs. W. Kilbey
SEND Governor: Miss D. Mortimer

PE and School Sport
Vision for PE
At Enmore C of E Primary School our vision for PE is to provide our children with a balanced curriculum that is inclusive and rich in the experiences it offers. We want all children to leave Enmore with a lifelong love and enjoyment of physical activity and sport which they take with them into adolescence and adulthood, as well as an understanding of the positive impact physical activity can have on their physical and mental health and wellbeing. Our school values are at the heart of all we do at Enmore and in PE these allow all children to develop themselves as an individual while building their confidence, resilience and leadership skills, as they succeed and excel in an encouraging and supportive environment.
2025/26
Bridgwater Schools' Dodgeball Tournament
Our other Mixed Dodgeball team took part in a tournament against large and small Bridgwater schools. A fantastic opportunity for them to gain more experience on the court!
West of England Dodgeball Competition
One of our Mixed Dodgeball teams travelled to Bristol to compete in the West of England Dodgeball competition. After battling it out against a number of schools, they finished second overall!
KS1 Football Festival
Twenty children from KS1 went to the football festival held at Bridgwater College. The children took part in a number of round-robin football activities with children from other schools.
Girls' South West Regional Dodgeball Finals
The Girls' Dodgeball team travelled to Weston-Super-Mare to compete in the South West Regional Dodgeball Finals. A fantastic day for all involved!
Year 1/2 Key Step Gymnastics
The children learnt a gymnastic routine in PE which they then performed against other schools for the Key Step Gymnastics competition.
Year 5/6 Tag Rugby Tournament
The Year 5/6 Tag Rugby team competed in a tournament at Brymore against a number of other schools. After playing brilliantly, they finished first in the small schools' tournament!
Girls' Football Match
The girls' football team played in their first ever match against Nether Stowey Primary School.
Year 5/6 County Sportshall Athletics
The Year 5/6 Sportshall Athletics team took part in the county final at Richard Huish College. After a hard fought morning, they finished first overall!
Year 4 Sportshall Athletics
Year 4 took part in the Year 4 Sportshall Athletics tournament at Bridgwater College. They competed against a number of small and large Bridgwater schools and finished first!
House Swimming Gala
After finishing their term of swimming, the children in Years 4 and 5 took part in the House Swimming Gala. Coleridge and Blake House tied for first place!
KS1 Athletics Festival
Twenty children from KS1 took part in the first festival of the year. 180 children from Bridgwater schools came together to take part in fun athletics activities. After lots of throwing and jumping, they took part in a number of relay races.
Year 5/6 Sportshall Athletics Tournament
In October, the Sportshall athletics team went to Bridgwater College to compete in the small school's competition. They finished first and qualified for the county finals.
Year 5/6 ESFA Football Tournament
The Year 5/6 Football team took part in a tournament against other local small schools. They finished 1st, qualifying for the county final.
Girls' Football Festival
The girl's football team went to a football festival at Berrow School.
2024/25
Year 5 Friendly Netball
The Year 5 netballers had a great time playing against St Joseph's. We played 7 a side and 3 matches. We won all 3 and gained some valuable experience. We also had the opportunity to play End Ball to gain passing and teamwork experience. We are ready for next season!
Year 6 Netball Tournament
The final tournament of our competitive season. A fabulous effort with 2 draws and 1 win against other Bridgwater schools at Bridgwater College Academy.
Year 5/6 Netball County Final
A hard-fought afternoon of County Finals netball at Taunton Vale. We played the top Bridgwater and Taunton teams and demonstrated our grit, determination and exemplary sportsmanship! Unfortunately, it wasn't filled with victory. Baskets were scored, possession won and lessons learned. Well done, Team Enmore! We are so proud of you.
KS1 Football Festival
Twenty children from KS1 went to the football festival held at Bridgwater College. The children took part in a number of round-robin football activities with children from other schools.
Year 5/6 Netball Tournament
The Year 5/6 Netball team entered the Bridgwater tournament on the 19th of March at Bridgwater College. We played 4 matches, had 3 Wins and 1 Loss. We qualified for the County Final on the 24th of April.
Year 5/6 Tag Rugby Tournament

Curriculum
The Content and Organisation of the Curriculum
The curriculum to which each child is entitled has been laid down by the National Curriculum, ensuring the development of a child moving through the school. The subjects of Religious Education, English, Mathematics, Science, Art, History, Geography, Music, Physical Education, I.C.T. and Design and Technology form the content of the curriculum.
In addition to the above the school curriculum also addresses cross-curricular issues such as Personal and Social Education, and Multi-cultural Education. This includes a developing understanding of British Values and how children can keep themselves safe. The manner in which the curriculum as a whole is delivered will reflect the needs of each individual child, and so the organisation of teaching groups will, of necessity, be flexible. Children will be taught at various times, as a whole class, as a matched or mixed ability group and individually.
Subjects are usually taught discretely. Early synthetic phonics is taught through the Read, Write Inc. phonics scheme and early reading is supported through the Oxford Reading Tree.
It is important to note that the requirements of the National Curriculum do not apply to children who are not of statutory school age, i.e. “rising fives”. They follow the Foundation Stage Curriculum which prepares them for the National Curriculum and for their later years in the school.
Religious Education and Collective Worship
Religious Education in our school is in accordance with the locally agreed syllabus and reflects the teaching of the Church of England. Through the teaching of religious education we aim to promote the spiritual and moral development of the children, at the same time seeking to ensure that it promotes respect, understanding and tolerance for those who adhere to different faiths. A parent does have the right to withdraw their child from religious education if so wished.
In order to comply with the 1988 Education Reform Act each school is required to ensure that all pupils take part in daily collective worship. Nothing in the Education Reform Act affects parents’ rights, as established in the 1944 Act. Any parent does have the right to withdraw their child from collective worship if they wish.
